import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 590

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/590](https://www.erdosproblems.com/590)
 - [Ch72] Chang, C. C., A partition theorem for the complete graph on {$\omega\sp{\omega }$}. J. Combinatorial Theory Ser. A (1972), 396-452.
 - [Sp57] Specker, Ernst, Teilmengen von Mengen mit Relationen. Comment. Math. Helv. (1957), 302-314.
 - [La73] Larson, Jean A., A short proof of a partition theorem for the ordinal {$\omega \sp{\omega }$}. Ann. Math. Logic (1973/74), 129-145.
-/

open Cardinal Ordinal

namespace Erdos590

universe u

/--
Let $α$ be the infinite ordinal $\omega^{\omega}$. It was proved by Chang [Ch72] that any red/blue
colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3]
theorem erdos_590 : OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ ω) (ω ^ ω) 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Specker [Sp57] proved that when $α=ω^2$ any red/blue
colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3]
theorem erdos_590.variants.two : OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ 2) (ω ^ 2) 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Specker [Sp57] proved that when $α=ω^n$ for $3≤ n < \omega$ then it is not the case that any
red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3]
theorem erdos_590.variants.ge_three_false {n : ℕ} (h : 3 ≤ n) :
    ¬ OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ n) (ω ^ n) 3 := by
  sorry

/--
Let m be a finite cardinal $< \omega$. Let $α$ be the infinite ordinal $\omega^{\omega}$.
It was proved by Milnor that any red/blue colouring of the edges of $K_α$ there is either a
red $K_α$ or a blue $K_3$. A shorter proof was found by Larson [La73]
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3]
theorem erdos_590.variants.finite_cardinal (m : ℕ) : OrdinalCardinalRamsey (ω ^ ω) (ω ^ ω) m := by
  sorry

end Erdos590

findings.description: The Lean statement correctly has blue target cardinality `m`, but its docstring says “a blue $K_3$”. This repeats the main theorem instead of describing the arbitrary-finite-target variant.
findings.source_evidence: Džamonja–Koutsoukou-Argyraki–Paulson, arXiv:2011.13218v3, §§2–3, explicitly state the Milner–Larson result: “For all m ∈ ℕ, ω^ω → (ω^ω, m)”, citing Larson [La73]. https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.13218
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “a blue $K_3$” with “a blue $K_m$” in this docstring. Leave the Lean proposition unchanged.

findings.description: The docstring attributes the finite-target extension to “Milnor”. The mathematician responsible was E. C. (Eric) Milner. This is an attribution error, not an error in the proposition.
findings.source_evidence: Džamonja–Koutsoukou-Argyraki–Paulson, arXiv:2011.13218v3, §2: “In an unpublished manuscript, Eric Milner improved Chang's result” to all natural-number targets; §3 calls it the “unpublished result by E.C. Milner” proved in Larson's cited paper. https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.13218

reformulations.difference: The conventional ordinal partition relation uses order types for both monochromatic targets. `OrdinalCardinalRamsey` instead uses two complementary simple graphs and measures the blue target by cardinality. The same encoding is used in all four declarations.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Complementarity is equivalent to `blue = redᶜ`, so the graph quantifiers describe exactly red/blue colourings of unordered pairs. `α.ToType` has order type α. For a subset s of this well-order and any m : ℕ, `#s = (m : Cardinal)` iff `typeLT s = (m : Ordinal)`, by `Ordinal.card_type` and `Ordinal.card_eq_nat`. Thus no order-type information is lost for these finite blue targets. A generic ↔ to the single-graph formulation with ordinal targets was proved as `ramsey_iff_ordinal_blue` in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: Džamonja, Koutsoukou-Argyraki and Paulson, Formalising Ordinal Partition Relations Using Isabelle/HOL, arXiv:2011.13218v3, especially §§2–3; abstract https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.13218 and LaTeX source https://arxiv.org/e-print/2011.13218.

Specker, Teilmengen von Mengen mit Relationen, Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici 31 (1956–1957), especially pp. 302–303, Satz 3 on p. 310, and the final remarks on p. 314. Full text: https://www.e-periodica.ch/cntmng?pid=com-001%3A1956%3A31%3A%3A16&bot=1 ; archival DOI 10.5169/seals-515706.
https://api.elsevier.com/content/article/PII:0003484373900065?httpAccept=text/xml — Larson article metadata, not full text.
https://people.clas.ufl.edu/jal/selected-publications/ — Larson's bibliography; the linked preprints were marked removed.
Local Mathlib sources: Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Basic.lean and Clique.lean; SetTheory/Ordinal/Basic.lean and Exponential.lean; SetTheory/Cardinal/Basic.lean; Order/BooleanAlgebra/Basic.lean.
review.notes: No mathematical misformalization found in the four propositions. Specker's primary text confirms the ω² result and the negative result for every finite exponent at least 3. The accessible arXiv paper explicitly states Chang's theorem and the Milner–Larson extension. Lean checks verified the encoding, the negated relation's quantifier structure, natural versus finite-ordinal exponentiation, satisfiability of complementarity, and the harmless m = 0, 1, 2 cases. Both scratch files compiled without errors or warnings. Access limitation: erdosproblems.com/590 remained blocked by Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers, and the original Chang/Larson full texts were inaccessible; their exact statements were checked through the cited scholarly overview. Current main-problem status was independently checked in the Erdős problem database. The reviewed file still matches the requested commit byte-for-byte.
